description: Strings, character arrays and string handling functions in C

questions.questionText: How are strings represented in C?
questions.optionA: As a special string data type
questions.optionB: As character arrays terminated by a null character
questions.explanation: C does not have a built-in string data type. Strings are stored as character arrays ending with the null character '\0'.

questions.questionText: Which character marks the end of a string in C?
questions.explanation: The null character '\0' marks the end of a C string.

questions.questionText: Which header file is required for functions such as strlen(), strcpy() and strcmp()?
questions.explanation: String handling functions such as strlen, strcpy and strcmp are declared in string.h.

questions.questionText: Which is the correct declaration of a character array that can store a string of up to 9 characters?
questions.explanation: One extra element is required for the terminating '\0', so 10 characters of storage are needed for a 9-character string.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? char str[] = "Hello"; printf("%s", str);
questions.explanation: The %s format specifier prints the complete null-terminated string.

questions.questionText: What is the length of the string "Hello" returned by strlen()?
questions.explanation: Hello contains 5 visible characters. strlen() does not count the terminating '\0'.

questions.questionText: Which function is used to find the length of a string?
questions.explanation: strlen() returns the number of characters in a null-terminated string, excluding '\0'.

questions.questionText: Which function copies one string into another?
questions.explanation: The strcpy() function copies the string pointed to by the source into the destination array.

questions.questionText: Which function compares two strings lexicographically?
questions.explanation: strcmp() compares two strings character by character.

questions.questionText: What does strcmp() return when two strings are equal?
questions.explanation: strcmp() returns 0 when the two strings are equal.

questions.questionText: Which function is used to concatenate two strings?
questions.explanation: strcat() appends the source string to the end of the destination string.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? char a[20] = "Hello"; char b[] = " World"; strcat(a, b); printf("%s", a);
questions.explanation: strcat() appends b to a, producing Hello World.

questions.questionText: Which format specifier is commonly used with scanf() to read a word into a character array?
questions.explanation: The %s conversion specifier is used to read a string up to whitespace.

questions.questionText: What is a limitation of scanf("%s", str) when reading a string?
questions.explanation: scanf with %s skips leading whitespace and then reads characters until the next whitespace.

questions.questionText: Which function is generally preferred for safely reading a line of text into a character array?
questions.explanation: fgets() allows a maximum number of characters to be specified and is preferred over the unsafe gets().

questions.questionText: Which function prints a string followed by a newline?
questions.explanation: puts() writes a string to standard output and appends a newline.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? char str[] = "ABC"; printf("%c", str[1]);
questions.explanation: String indexing starts at 0, so str[1] is the second character, B.

questions.questionText: What is the value of str[3] in char str[] = "ABC"?
questions.explanation: The characters are stored at indexes 0, 1 and 2. Index 3 contains the terminating null character.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? char str[] = "C Programming"; printf("%zu", strlen(str));
questions.explanation: C Programming contains 13 characters including the space.

questions.questionText: Which function can be used to convert a lowercase character to uppercase?
questions.explanation: toupper() from ctype.h converts a lowercase character to its uppercase equivalent when applicable.

questions.questionText: Which header file contains character classification functions such as isdigit() and isalpha()?
questions.explanation: Character classification and conversion functions such as isdigit(), isalpha() and toupper() are declared in ctype.h.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? char str[20] = "Hello"; strcpy(str, "C"); printf("%s", str);
questions.explanation: strcpy() replaces the destination string with the source string, so str becomes C.

questions.questionText: What will strcmp("abc", "abc") return?
questions.explanation: strcmp() returns 0 when both strings contain the same sequence of characters.

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of the null character '\0' in a C string?
questions.optionA: It converts the string to uppercase
questions.optionD: It marks the end of the string
questions.explanation: The null character tells string functions where the character sequence ends.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? char str[] = "Hello"; int i = 0; while(str[i] != '\0') { i++; } printf("%d", i);
questions.explanation: The loop stops when it reaches '\0'. There are 5 characters before the null character, so i becomes 5.
